title: Standard Treatment Guidelines for Secondary Care: Acute Coronary Syndrome and Ischemic Heart Disease
author_or_organization: Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India
date_uncertainty_note: DGHS national secondary care clinical guideline.

passages.text: Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) encompasses unstable angina, non-ST elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI). Typical ischemic pain is described as substernal heaviness, squeezing, aching, or crushing pressure, lasting more than 20 minutes. The pain frequently radiates to the left shoulder, left arm, neck, throat, or lower jaw. In elderly, female, or diabetic patients, presentation may be atypical with fatigue or epigastric discomfort.

The coexistence of chest discomfort with dyspnea (shortness of breath), cold clammy diaphoresis, unexplained presyncope or syncope, profound nausea, or hypotension marks an acute high-risk presentation. Concurrent thoracic chest pain and dyspnea represents acute cardiopulmonary compromise requiring immediate emergency triage.

Stable angina pectoris presents with predictable chest tightness induced by physical exercise or cold exposure, which subsides completely within 5 to 10 minutes of resting or sublingual nitroglycerin. In contrast, ACS manifests with chest discomfort occurring at rest or with minimal exertion, lasting > 20 minutes, or exhibiting an accelerating crescendo pattern of increasing frequency and severity.

Any patient presenting with suspected acute ischemic chest pain or high-risk red-flag symptoms must be directed immediately to an emergency department. Mandatory initial emergency measures include acquiring a 12-lead ECG within 10 minutes of presentation, continuous cardiac rhythm monitoring, pulse oximetry, and intravenous access. Outpatient delay or unsupervised self-medication is hazardous.
